name: Congenital Axonal Neuropathy with Encephalopathy
aliases: Congenital Axonal Neuropathy Type with Encephalopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Axonal Neuropathy with Encephalopathy

criteria.description: Early-onset hypotonia and severe motor developmental delay with encephalopathy
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced nerve conduction velocities
MRI showing cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination consistent with encephalopathy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with axonal neuropathy and encephalopathy
Exclusion of acquired causes of neuropathy and encephalopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: clinical presentation, electrophysiology consistent with axonal neuropathy, and brain imaging showing encephalopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; exclusion of acquired causes is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe muscle weakness present from birth
searchTerms: congenital muscle weakness and absent reflexes
worsening brain disease with delayed milestones
progressive brain dysfunction with developmental delay
declining brain function and slow development

pathognomonic.symptomName: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy confirmed by nerve conduction studies
searchTerms: nerve conduction tests showing axon loss
nerve damage affecting movement and sensation
muscle wasting mainly in hands and feet
weakness and shrinkage of muscles farthest from center

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to bulbar weakness
searchTerms: difficulty feeding due to swallowing weakness
problems eating from weak throat muscles
bulbar muscle weakness causing feeding issues
recurrent seizures or epileptic brain disease

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency secondary to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory failure due to muscle weakness
slow brain nerve insulation on MRI
delayed myelin formation in brain scans
reduced sensation in arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Joint contractures due to muscle imbalance
searchTerms: joint tightening due to muscle problems
contracted joints caused by uneven muscle strength

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein without pleocytosis
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral atrophy and delayed myelination
Nerve MRI may show nerve root hypertrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as MFN2, GDAP1, or other axonal neuropathy-associated genes
Variants associated with mitochondrial dysfunction reported
other: Electromyography showing reduced amplitude of motor and sensory potentials consistent with axonal neuropathy
Nerve biopsy demonstrating loss of large myelinated fibers

redFlags: Severe hypotonia with absent reflexes at birth
Respiratory failure requiring early ventilatory support
